test_title: PYST 1: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - English Language (Held On 24 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:

The house had been painted by the workers before the rain started.

options.text: The workers had painted the house before the rain started.
The workers painted the house before the rain started.
The house was painted before the rain started.
The workers have painted the house before the rain started.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Active voice structure: The agent (the doer of the action) becomes the subject of the sentence.
 
• In the passive voice, the sentence is: "The house had been painted by the workers before the rain started."
 
• The sentence is in the **Past Perfect** tense. The passive form is *had + been + V3*. To convert it to active voice, the structure is: *Subject + had + V3 + Object*.
 
• To convert to active voice: Place the agent "the workers" at the beginning as the subject.
 
• Change the passive verb "had been painted" to the active form "had painted."
 
• Place the original subject "the house" after the verb as the object.
 
• The subordinate clause "before the rain started" remains unchanged.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The workers had painted the house before the rain started."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"The workers painted the house..." – Incorrect because it changes the tense to Past Simple.
 
• **Option 3: **"The house was painted..." – Incorrect because it is still in the passive voice and changes the tense to Past Simple.
 
• **Option 4: **"The workers have painted the house..." – Incorrect because it changes the tense to Present Perfect.
